warning_signs_missed: 2026-06-19 - On day 3 she asked, in writing and with unusual precision, how the paid-traffic handover would work. We answered with a date and no plan. Everything that followed is downstream of that unwritten answer; a client who asks a structured question about the core deliverable is telling you where she will judge you.

2026-06-26 - We swapped her account manager mid-complaint with no introduction and no handover message. Her open question then sat until she wrote 'Why when i ask no one answer'. A silent personnel change is a churn accelerant and there is no rule requiring a handover note.

2026-06-28 - We switched off the only acquisition that was working on a verbal 'Yes there will be', and deleted her already-queued posts by mistake. From that day nobody on our side ever looked at her fan-growth numbers. The absence of a metric was itself the warning.

2026-07-01 - She asked twice for a whale list and a mass-DM pause and received no reply at all. Total silence on a request about her own top spenders' trust is a louder signal than any complaint, and it was invisible because nothing tracks unanswered messages.

2026-07-03 - She found out about a $700 sale from the fan, not from us. When a client learns what her agency is doing via her own Snapchat, our process has become invisible to her - and we never fixed it, so it happened again with a $1,000 custom on 8/4.

2026-07-09 - 'if you're selling calls, I need to have all information beforehand. Otherwise , I'm not going to do the calls.' That is a stated condition of continuing to work. It was read as a complaint, not as terms, and never turned into a briefing template.

2026-07-24 - She was locked out of her own OnlyFans accounts by our Infloww change and the reply was to ask if she had changed her password. Being locked out of your own business by your agency is a five-alarm trust event; it was closed in three messages and never written up.

2026-08-01 - A broadcast apology promising 'plenty of updates starting next week' bought a week of patience and was followed by nothing. An apology not followed by account-specific delivery converts a patient client into a leaving one, and we had no mechanism to notice the promise had come due.

2026-08-10 - 'it's already been 2 months' and 'getting worse and worse' is a written churn warning in plain language. Nobody flagged the account, nobody called her, and the owner's promised one-hour update never came. Eight days later she left.

2026-08-11 / 08-14 / 08-17 - The same complaint screenshotted three times in six days, closed each time with an assertion and no data. She terminated roughly 18 hours after the third 'Yes all solved'. Any complaint asked a third time should have auto-escalated to the owner that day.
top_fix: Ban closing a client complaint with an assertion - require a number, a screenshot or a dated commitment, and auto-escalate to a named owner the second time the same complaint is raised. Vicky's three highest-stakes threads (replacement traffic, the mermaidua page, and the undelivered $700 call) were each closed with 'its live', 'Yes all solved' and 'we are managing him', with no evidence behind any of them; she terminated roughly 18 hours after the third bare assertion. The same rule would have caught the account on 8/14 at the latest, and it is the one change that generalises to every other client in this book.
